what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: The list I send by email is people's first page
sections.para: Reading lists shipped on 11 October and the agent at agent@riskmandate.ai now builds them into my emails, about twenty by 18 October. Most recipients meet the newsroom through one, so since 21 October the page opens as a letter, explains itself, shows what was read and was reviewed by the Designer first.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Nine lines: lists, the agent, the first page, the redesign
sections.para: A list is a link from me to one person; the agent builds them and I send them. For most readers it is the first page they see, so it now opens as a letter, uses the screen, shows what was read in five views, was reviewed before release, and points at signed answers next.

sections.label: A link from me to one person
sections.line: A list is numbers, names and a note after the #
sections.para: I asked on 11 October for a way to send one person the articles to read in order, and it shipped the same day as v0.8.0. The list lives after the #, so the server never sees who sent it to whom, and it opens as a persona the reader can keep or remove.

sections.label: The agent builds them into my emails
sections.line: The agent builds each list; I read and send the email
sections.para: The agent behind agent@riskmandate.ai reads the thread, picks articles by number, writes a line on why, builds the link and checks it on the live site. Its 18 October debrief counts about 20 lists among 178 emails, each waiting in my drafts until I sent it.

sections.label: The first page they see
sections.line: For most recipients, the list is the newsroom's first page
sections.para: People arrive from an email, often through a wrapped link, and the list is the first page they see. The first version, a narrow column of links, did not say what the site was, what 10p meant, or what to do, and the first article sat below the fold.

sections.label: A letter, not a list
sections.line: Since 21 October it opens as a letter and explains
sections.para: A dateline, my note signed, and one line on what the list holds and costs open the page. The first article is a large card with a legible picture, the rest two to a row, and a side column explains the newsroom in four steps lit in turn.

sections.label: What you have read, on the list
sections.line: The list shows what you read, from your own browser
sections.para: A ring, section bars, the time left and what was spent come from the reader's own browser, and Continue goes to the first unread section. Done, later and not for me are the vault pane's own notes, and the list catches up when another tab reads.

sections.label: Five ways to see the same list
sections.line: Five views: cards, headlines, sections, pictures, the graph
sections.para: The same list can be seen as cards, as headlines with one-liners, as every section in a line ticked as read, as the articles' figures, or as a graph of ideas, links and the articles beyond the list. The page remembers the reader's choice.

sections.label: Reviewed before it shipped
sections.line: The Designer found fourteen problems; all were fixed
sections.para: Before release the newsroom's Designer reviewed a real list in every view at two widths. The worst findings were a hidden keep and remove box, no headline above the fold, a dashboard of zeros, illegible pictures and decisions before headlines; all fourteen were fixed and the review is published.

sections.label: Pages that people use have to keep up
sections.line: Pages people use have to keep up with the site
sections.para: The page for publishers went stale within a week and is now rebuilt every release with its own version history; the reading list is the second such page. Old links still work, because a list is only numbers and names, so every recipient gets the newest page.

sections.label: What comes back
sections.line: Next: answers from the page, signed, back to me
sections.para: Lists go out easily; answers come back only by email. The plan is notes from the page that reach me and the agent, using the readers' existing notes and lane and the key pairs of pki.sgit.ai, plus a view chosen by the sender and a picture for the email.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: No open counts; one agent's count; a proposal
sections.para: There is no record of opens by design; the twenty is the agent's count of 18 October; the screenshots use an example list; reading shows per browser unless the vault is used; the Designer is an agent role; signed answers are not built.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A memo of 24 October, the release and the debrief
sections.para: My voice memo of 24 October, written up by this site's agent; the brief of 11 October and v0.8.0; release v0.13.19, card 086 and the Designer's review; the inbox agent's debrief of 18 October; screenshots of an example list at 1440 and 390 pixels wide.
